UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY
FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK
IN THE MATTER OF No. 2001 - 02
ANGELINA PLETT
ASSESSMENT OF CIVIL MONEY PENALTIES
AGAINST ANGELINA PLETT
I. INTRODUCTION
The Secretary of the United States Department of the Treasury has delegated to
the Director of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (“FinCEN”) the authority to
determine whether a financial institution has violated the Bank Secrecy Act, 31 U.S.C.
§§5311 et seq. and 31 CFR Part 103 thereunder (“BSA”), and what, if any, sanction is
appropriate.
II. JURISDICTION
Angelina Plett (“Plett”) was, at all relevant times, an owner and the manager of
Cash For Checks Inc. (“Cash For Checks”). Cash For Checks was, at all relevant times, a
licensed check casher located in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma and was a “financial
institution” within the meaning of 31 U.S.C. §5312(a)(2) and 31 CFR §103.11(n).1
III. FINCEN’S DETERMINATIONS
A. Structuring
FinCEN has determined that between July 11, 1995, and April 26, 1996, Plett
willfully structured or willfully assisted in structuring check cashing transactions for
Joseph A. Sivigliano (“Sivigliano”) through a domestic financial institution in violation
of 31 U.S.C. §5324(a)(3) and 31 CFR §103.63(c). During the relevant time period,
Sivigliano cashed 136 checks totaling more than $1.17 million at Cash For Checks. On
each of 43 days, Sivigliano cashed a series of checks that individually totaled less than
$10,000, but that together exceeded $10,0

This reporting requirement applies to [e]ach person who physically transports ... or causes to be physically transported ... currency or other monetary instruments in an aggregate amount exceeding $10,000 at one time from the United States to any place outside the United States .... A person is deemed to have caused such transportation ... when he aids, abets, counsels, commands, procures, or requests it to be done by a financial institution or another person. 31 C.F.R. § 103.23 (2005). In fleshing out what it means for a person to transport currency “at one time,” 31 C.F.R. § 103.11 (2005) sets forth the following criteria: (1) That person either alone, in conjunction with or on behalf of others; (2) Transports, mails, ships or receives in any manner; is about to transport, mail or ship in any manner; or causes the transportation, mailing, shipment or receipt in any manner of; (3) Monetary instruments; (4) Into the United States or out of the United States; (5) Totaling more than $10,000; (6) (i) On one calendar day or (ii) if for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements of section 103.23

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: Neutral — 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade CTR reporting, but the facts do not show the deposits were structured to avoid a $10,000 CTR threshold or that the individual acted with the required purpose to evade reporting.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324(a)(3) makes it unlawful to “structure” or assist in structuring a transaction with one or more domestic financial institutions for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements of 31 U.S.C. § 5313(a) (CTR reporting, generally triggered by cash transactions >$10,000 in a day). Here, the fact pattern shows many inbound transactions labeled “smurfing fan-in deposit,” including multiple cash deposits under $10,000 (e.g., $9,972.06) across several days and counterparties, which is consistent with possible structuring. However, the record does not establish key elements: (1) that these cash deposits were made at/through a “domestic financial institution” subject to CTR filing, (2) whether any single-day aggregate cash activity exceeded $10,000 such that a CTR would have been required absent structuring, and (3) the required mens rea—i.e., that the individual acted “for the purpose of evading” CTR reporting rather than for some other reason. Because intent/purpose to evade and the CTR-triggering context are not shown, applicability of § 5324 prohibits structuring cannot be determined from the provided facts.
